title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' drafts axiomatize a tame, polyhedral-like topology combinatorially. There is a set M of elementary objects (cells). Each X in M has an elementary figure F_X, its closed cell with its faces. 𝓕 is the set of 'figures', which are finite sets of cells closed under faces, like simplicial or cell complexes. The basic relations are:
- sub-figure: G ⊂ F with G a figure.
- subdivision: F' subdivides F.
- refinement: G ≪ F iff G ⊂ F' for some subdivision F' of F. This is the definition on p.47; p.47 writes the relation the other way round, F ≪ G.
- compatibility: F ∪ G is again a figure.

Axiom C4 (p.47) has two parts. If G is a sub-figure of F and G' a subdivision of G, then G' ∪ (F∖G) is a subdivision of F. Moreover G' ∩ F ⊂ G: cells of the subdivision that are also cells of the ambient figure already lie in G. Hence every subdivision of a sub-figure is induced from one of the whole figure. Cor. 2 says that ≪ is an order relation.

This page:
- The crossed-out top lines are a discarded attempt at a proposition, using subdivision G' ∪ (F∖G).
- Cor. 3: for figures G, F, G ⊂ F iff (i) G is compatible with F and (ii) G ≪ F. Proof: put H = F ∪ G, a figure by compatibility, with F a sub-figure of H. Take a subdivision F' of F with G ⊂ F'. By C4, F' ∪ (H∖F), which the diagram writes as F' ∪ G, is a subdivision of H. By the second clause of C4, F' ∩ H ⊂ F. Since G ⊂ F' ∩ H, we get G ⊂ F.
- Special case for cells (X ∈ M, F ∈ 𝓕): X ∈ F iff X is compatible with F and X ≪ F. For X, Y ∈ M: X ≤ Y (face relation) iff X is compatible with Y and X ≪ Y. So the face order is recovered from compatibility plus refinement.
- Definition: F and G are disjoint if they are compatible and F ∩ G = ∅. Cells X, Y are disjoint if F_X and F_Y are, i.e. X and Y are compatible and no Z satisfies Z ≤ X and Z ≤ Y.
- NB: if F and G are disjoint, then any X ∈ F and Y ∈ G are disjoint; the converse is marked 'not evident'. Sub-figures of disjoint figures are disjoint.
- 'De plus' leads into C5 on p.49: disjointness is invariant under subdivision.

Purpose: building the elementary combinatorial calculus (order, compatibility, disjointness, induced subdivisions, gluing) needed to define a category of tame 'figures' up to subdivision, i.e. a combinatorial foundation of PL / 'topologie modérée'.
errors: Notation inconsistency: p.47 defines 'G raffinement de F' and writes F ≪ G. This page uses G ≪ F for 'G refines F'. The page's usage is the one that makes Cor. 3 read correctly.

Cor. 3's proof uses the second clause of C4 (G' ∩ F ⊂ G), which on p.47 is a marginal correction rather than part of the cleanly stated axiom. The proof is valid only with that clause included as an axiom.

In the NB, the passage from disjoint F, G to disjoint X ∈ F, Y ∈ G tacitly uses F_X ⊂ F and F_Y ⊂ G, i.e. figures are closed under faces. The converse fails in general because compatibility of F ∪ G is a global condition; Grothendieck correctly flags it as non-evident.

ideas.what: Characterization of sub-figure inclusion as compatibility plus refinement (Cor. 3), and recovery of the face order on cells from compatibility plus refinement
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial characterization of subcomplexes and face relations in an axiomatic PL / cell-complex framework
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore of PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Rourke–Sanderson) in concrete form; no standard axiomatic version

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures, defined as compatible with empty intersection, and its stability under passing to sub-figures (and, on the next page, to subdivisions)
Overall programme: axiomatize tame topology via cells, figures, subdivisions and compatibility rather than via point-set topology
ideas.modern_name: Tame topology ('topologie modérée'), close in spirit to o-minimal structures and to axiomatic polyhedral categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); the programme itself is Grothendieck's (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces tame topology in general terms; the cell/figure axiomatics here are not published to my knowledge

missed.claim: This is part of an unpublished, concrete combinatorial axiomatization of tame topology: cells M, figures 𝓕, subdivision, compatibility, with axioms C4–C7 and their corollaries. It differs from the o-minimal approach later adopted, and as far as I know it has not been reconstructed or analysed in print. This page itself contains only routine lemmas within that system.
missed.quote: Pour que G ⊂ F, il faut et il suffit que G compatible à F (i.e. F ∪ G une figure ...) et G ≪ F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The axiom system (C1–C7…) could be compared with o-minimal cell decomposition and with abstract polyhedral or 'cellular' categories, as a possible foundation for tame stratified spaces. The interest lies in the whole manuscript, not this page.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine elementary lemmas, a sub-figure criterion and a definition of disjointness, inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame-topology notes. The framework is historically interesting, but nothing on this page is a striking new result.
transcription_corrections: The arrow labelled C4 means 'F' ∩ H ⊂ F by the second clause of C4', i.e. G ⊂ F' ∩ H ⊂ F.
The vertical diagram reads: F ⊂ H = F ∪ G, with an upward arrow labelled 'subd.' from F' ∪ G. That is, F' ∪ G is a subdivision of H, via C4.
In the cell case, the second condition is 'X raffine F' (X ≪ F). The line for X, Y should read X ≤ Y ⟺ {X compat. à Y ; X ≪ Y}; the crossed-out word is a variant of 'raffine'.
The left marginal note reads roughly 'cas particulier de C4' / 'raison d'être de C4'.
The definition line should begin 'Deux F, G ∈ 𝓕 sont dites disjointes ...', with a marginal insertion '(X et Y disjoints ⇒ X et Y distincts)'.
